title: Build a memory palace for formulas
hook: Hang each formula on a spot in a place you know by heart, then walk through it to remember.

steps.prompt: Picture your home. From memory, name five things you pass walking from the front door to your bed, in order.
steps.answer: Anything works, like door, light switch, couch, hallway mirror, bed. A route you already know by heart is the frame of a memory palace.

steps.prompt: A memory palace (also called the method of loci) works because...
choices: Your memory for places and routes is strong, so you hang new facts on a route you already know
Places are easier to write down
It turns facts into a song
steps.why: People remember spaces and routes very well. Each stop gives a fact a fixed spot and a built-in order.

steps.prompt: Put the steps for building a memory palace in order.
items: Pick a place you know well
Choose a route through it with fixed stops
Turn each fact into a vivid image
Put one image at each stop
Walk the route in your head to recall them
steps.why: Place, route, images, placement, then practice walking it.

steps.prompt: Your first stop is your desk, and it holds the area of a circle, A = πr². Which image will stick best?
choices: The words "pi r squared" written on the desk
A pirate on your desk slicing a giant pie into a perfect square
A plain circle
steps.why: Vivid, strange and active images stick. Pie, pirate and square encode π, r and the squared.

steps.prompt: Stop 2 is your chair, and it holds a² + b² = c². Which image fits the method best?
choices: An ant on one square cushion and a bee on another, and together they flood the chair with a whole sea
The formula on a sticky note
A triangle drawn on the chair
steps.why: Ant (a), bee (b), sea (c), and squares for the squared: every part of the formula is in the picture.

steps.prompt: Leo's palace for geometry facts. Tap the stop that breaks the method.
lines: Front door: a glowing 45-45-90 sign with sides 1, 1 and √2
Hallway: a 30-60-90 triangle rug with sides 1, √3 and 2
Kitchen: he puts nothing there and just hopes he remembers the circle formulas
Bathroom: x² + y² = r² written in the fog on a round mirror
steps.why: Every fact needs an image at a stop. An empty stop gives you nothing to walk back to.

steps.prompt: On test day you blank on the volume of a cone. Using your palace, what do you do?
choices: Walk the route in your head to the stop where you put it
Guess
Skip every geometry question
steps.why: The route is the index. Walk it stop by stop until you reach the image.

keys: Use a route you know by heart; each stop holds one fact.
Make images vivid, strange and moving: a pirate slicing pie into squares.
To recall, walk the route in your head, stop by stop. Practice the walk a few times.

recall.prompt: What makes a memory palace work?
choices: Strong memory for places and routes
Repeating words out loud
Writing things neatly
recall.why: Facts hang on a route you already know.

choices: Something vivid, odd and moving
Plain words on a wall
A small, ordinary object
recall.why: Strange and active images are easier to find again.

recall.prompt: You forget a formula you stored. What do you do?
choices: Walk the route to its stop
Start a new palace
Give up
recall.why: The route takes you straight to it.
